messages:
incidentbot: 🚨 PagerDuty alert fired: `PD: metrics-scrape-failure` for prometheus-scrape-cluster-us-west. symptoms: multiple scrape errors (HTTP 504/503), exporter pod restarts, and downstream log-ingest queue growth. Auto-escalation target: eng-sre on-call.

mike.sre: acked. I'll start triage. seeing spike in scrape errors around 2026-03-15T14:12Z.

aisha_oncall: on call and looking. can someone check prometheus-exporter pods and scrape-proxy?

pagerduty-bot: @aisha_oncall — ack recorded (aisha_oncall). PagerDuty incident: INC123456. Escalation window in 8m if no resolution.

mike.sre: checked kubectl quickly — exporter pods in us-west-2c are OOMKilled and Restarting. not a full node oom but container memory spike. logs show repeated 5xx from upstream logstore.

mike.sre: paste: ```
kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=prometheus-exporter -o wide
NAME                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
prometheus-exporter-0                   2/2     Running   12         5d
prometheus-exporter-1                   1/2     CrashLoopBackOff  34  3h
```

mike.sre: exporter logs: ```
E0315 14:11:43 exporter.go:142] failed to scrape target "node-exporter:9100": upstream error: HTTP 502
E0315 14:11:43 exporter.go:160] retrying target after backoff
```

tomas_infra: sounds like upstream logstore is throttling and returning 5xx which causes exporter memory to spike (retries). can we temporarily route scrapes to replica region or reduce scrape frequency?

jenna_ops: customer impact: CloudDash dashboards for some enterprise customers show missing node_cpu metrics since ~14:10Z. Ops routed a notice to customer-ops channel to triage. severity: P2 for now but risk if dashboards stay blank.

aisha_oncall: can we silence PD noise while we mitigate? I'm going to add a 30m silence for the alert group, keep incident open.

mike.sre: doing quick mitigations: 1) cordon & drain exporter-1? i'd rather restart container first. 2) scale down scrape concurrency: update configmap to lower scrape_timeout and targets per worker.

mike.sre: running: ```
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/prometheus-exporter
kubectl -n monitoring exec -it prometheus-exporter-0 -- kill -HUP 1
```

incidentbot: PD silence applied by aisha_oncall for 30m.

tomas_infra: I've applied a temporary route in the scrape-proxy: set upstream to replica-logstore-us-east for the affected exporter group. this will reduce pressure on primary for 15m. changed proxy config: `upstream = ["logstore-us-east:9200"]` and reloaded.

mike.sre: after restart, exporter-1 back to Running (0 restarts in last 5m). scrape error rate down from 40% -> 6%.

ryan_ml: FYI, model-serving dashboards were showing increased input latency correlated with missing metrics — looks like our autoscaler used cpu metrics that were missing and scaled conservatively. I'll temporarily pin replicas for the model-pool.

jenna_ops: customer-ops notified enterprise-188 / infra-team-ops. they reported dashboards recovering slowly. asking for timeline to full recovery.

aisha_oncall: timeline: mitigation applied, scrapes reduced, failover upstream, restart completed. continue monitoring for 30m. reassigning PD incident to sre-postmortem if issue reappears.

mike.sre: follow-up actions: - propose increasing exporter request/limits to avoid OOM on transient upstream errors - add circuit-breaker on exporter to stop aggressive retries - update scrape-proxy failover to rotate upstreams automatically - create PD rule to aggregate repeated exporter failures into single incident to reduce fanout

tomas_infra: adding an emergency metric: `scrape_error_rate{job="prometheus-exporter"}` and dashboard panel to show exporter restart counts. also pushed a k8s HorizontalPodAutoscaler tweak: lower downscale aggressiveness.

incidentbot: PD incident INC123456 resolved (auto-close) — resolved by: aisha_oncall.

mike.sre: confirmed metrics back to normal. node_cpu, node_mem series returning. log-ingest queue length trending down.

jenna_ops: marking customer impact: partial (dashboards delayed ~20-30m for some customers), no data loss. Notifying account managers for customers affected.

aisha_oncall: adding postmortem ticket: PMT-2026-035. tagging owners: @tomas_infra, @mike.sre, @ryan_ml. Please add timelines and root cause analysis.

mike.sre: quick note for postmortem: root cause appears to be upstream logstore transient overload causing exporter retries and memory blowup. contributing factor: aggressive exporter retry/backoff policy and scrape-proxy single-primary config.

tomas_infra: will draft remediation PR for circuit-breaker + proxy failover and memory request bump. aiming to ship hotfix in next deploy window unless we need immediate patch.

ryan_ml: I'll handle autoscaler workaround for model-serving and remove pin after metrics are stable.

jenna_ops: closing loop with customer-ops, they'll send a short incident summary to affected accounts.

mike.sre: thanks all — good triage. leaving a watch for 2h. react if anything flips. :thumbsup:
